- Overestimate prices after strong positive sentiment spikes; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% if sentiment > 0.8 in recent days.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently low (<0.4) over last 5–7 days; add 3–5% to forecast if sentiment < 0.3.
- Lagged overreaction: if model forecast shows sharp drop after recent spike, adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence to historical range.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising; cap forecast at +5% above 14-day moving average for first 7 days.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” bias: if sentiment is high but price drops sharply, reduce forecast by 5–8% for next 3 days to avoid overconfidence in sentiment-driven momentum.
